designSummary: Two-group pragmatic trial, individual allocation stratified by practice; primary analysis by intention to treat.
sampleSize: The smallest difference worth detecting is 4 points on the index (claim c2), with a standard deviation of change of 8 points from the validation study. For 80 percent power at two-sided alpha 0.05, 63 dogs per group are needed for an unadjusted comparison; adjusting for the baseline score with an assumed correlation of 0.5 reduces this to about 48 per group. Allowing 20 percent loss to follow-up (retention of 78 percent in practice-based trials) gives 60 per group, 120 dogs, which matches about 20 enrolments a month for six months.
primaryAnalysis: Linear regression of six-month index score on group, adjusted for baseline score and practice (stratification factor), by intention to treat; 95 percent confidence interval for the adjusted difference.
secondaryAnalysis: Same model for percentage weight change and blinded lameness score; proportion with a pain relief reduction; clinic attendance described; hunger behaviours by group.
missingData: Multiple imputation of missing six-month scores using baseline score, practice, age and attendance, with a sensitivity analysis assuming worse outcomes in dogs lost to follow-up.
multiplicity: One primary outcome; secondary outcomes reported with confidence intervals and not used to claim effectiveness.
software: R; statistical analysis plan filed with the ethics committee before the first dog is enrolled.
overfittingGuards: Three adjustment covariates fixed in advance
No subgroup claims beyond a pre-specified practice-size interaction
summary: 120 dogs give 80 percent power for a 4-point difference after baseline adjustment and 20 percent loss.
